# Agentbox

> One inbox for a team and its agents, free and open source. Teammates' messages and the work Claude Code and Codex agents finish land in the same list, threads and the files agents make are handed between people with the work attached, and every task gets its own git worktree. Runs on an existing Claude or Codex subscription, with no server, no account and no API key. macOS app, or `npx agentbox-app` in a browser on any platform with Node 22.

Licence: GPL-3.0. Source: https://github.com/savannahfeder/agentbox

## Pages

- [Agentbox](https://agentbox.ac/): one inbox for teammates and agents, handing off threads and files, the team pages, every harness, and Agentcloud.
- [How to run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel](https://agentbox.ac/run-multiple-claude-code-agents): the four approaches, 23 tools compared with licences and commit dates, a measurement of what three agents at once actually costs, and 14 questions answered.
- [Is there a GUI for Claude Code?](https://agentbox.ac/claude-code-gui): Anthropic ships one, the Code tab in the Claude desktop app, with parallel sessions and optional git worktree isolation. The 21 third-party front ends beside it, which run on Windows and Linux, and when each is still worth running.
- [Claude Code and git worktrees](https://agentbox.ac/claude-code-worktrees): every command with its gotcha, why a new worktree has no node_modules or .env, what .worktreeinclude does, where each tool puts them, and a worked example from three agents to merged.
- [Conductor alternatives](https://agentbox.ac/conductor-alternative): 22 alternatives, which are open source, which run on Windows and Linux, why Agentbox is free, and when Conductor is the better buy.
- [Vibe Kanban is sunsetting. Where to go next](https://agentbox.ac/vibe-kanban-alternative): what happened, how to keep running it anyway, which boards are still maintained, and how to judge a replacement so it does not repeat.
- [Claude Code tools](https://agentbox.ac/claude-code-tools): a directory of 52 tools in six categories (orchestrators, status lines, usage and cost, monitors, hooks, skills and guides), each with licence, stars and last commit date read from the GitHub API.

## Notes for anyone quoting these pages

Every comparison carries the date it was checked and names the cases where a competing tool is the better choice. Star counts, licences, platforms and commit dates come from the GitHub API on the day of writing, not from other articles, and the tables are generated from that data rather than typed.

As of 17 October 2026: Vibe Kanban is sunsetting, announced 10 April 2026. Crystal is deprecated in favour of Nimbalyst. Terragon is dead. cmux has become a macOS terminal rather than an agent orchestrator. All four are still recommended by articles published this year, so check a last-commit date before trusting any list in this category, including this one.

One agent answering a question about a real repository took 16.4 seconds, and three agents started together took 17.1 seconds in total. The waits overlap, so running several at once is close to free. The tasks were small and read-only on purpose, the machine was under a load average between 12 and 19, and runs at six and ten agents are not finished yet.

Agentbox is three weeks old with 78 GitHub stars, which is the smallest project in its own comparison tables. Orca has 95,206. Where another tool is the better answer, the pages say so.
